nodes.label: Buy Without Defeat

nodes.label: Competition Structure Determinism
nodes.rationale: The report finds a recent geopolitical concentration in this promoted model.

nodes.label: Crisis Deduction Chain
nodes.rationale: The report records a verified-count mismatch and identifies this model as a promoted candidate.

nodes.label: AI Reforming Investment

nodes.label: Industry Belief Before Technical Signals
nodes.rationale: A verified fundamental change in competitiveness can outweigh an adverse technical signal for a medium- to long-term industry target.

nodes.label: Fundamental Competitiveness Change
nodes.rationale: Examples in the document are entry into a top global supply chain or receiving international certification.

nodes.label: External Verification of Change
nodes.rationale: The change must be externally verifiable, such as through supply-chain certification, a patent, or a customer announcement.

nodes.label: Adverse Technical Signal
nodes.rationale: The stated signals include a top divergence, a technical breakdown, or falling below a moving average.

nodes.label: Short-Term Sentiment Target
nodes.rationale: The document excludes short-term sentiment-driven targets, where technical and sentiment stop-loss discipline remains applicable.

nodes.label: Fundamental Thesis Falsification
nodes.rationale: A falsified fundamental thesis triggers the paired stop-loss discipline regardless of technical tolerance.

nodes.label: Layered Application by Target Type
nodes.rationale: The document reconciles prior rejection of pure technical analysis with active buying at a loss by separating sentiment targets from industry-certainty targets.

nodes.label: Leverage Cleanup Line
nodes.rationale: For a leverage-driven cycle stock, the prior leverage start price serves as a quantitative reference line for cleanup.

nodes.label: Leverage Start Point
nodes.rationale: The method first identifies the starting point of the previous leverage-driven move.

nodes.label: Leverage Peak
nodes.rationale: The method then identifies the peak of the leverage move before evaluating the decline.

nodes.label: Business Operations Unchanged
nodes.rationale: The document treats a stable and growing business as a required validation after leverage cleanup.

nodes.label: Leverage-Driven Cycle Stock
nodes.rationale: The stated applicable scope is cyclical sectors with observable leverage-funding traces and a clear start-to-peak-to-decline sequence.

nodes.label: Staged Position Building With Stop-Loss
nodes.rationale: After the method's checks, the stated decision is to build a position in stages and set a stop-loss rather than treat cleanup as an unconditional buy signal.

nodes.label: Liquidity-Driven Selloff
nodes.rationale: The document groups leveraged selling, ETF redemption, panic, and sector rotation as liquidity-driven causes that do not themselves impair operating cash flow.

nodes.label: Logic-Driven Selloff
nodes.rationale: The document groups lost orders, worsening competition, policy reversal, and management distrust as causes that undermine the earnings foundation.

nodes.label: Business Operations
nodes.rationale: Orders, revenue, and profit are the stated operational checks for distinguishing liquidity pressure from deterioration in logic.

nodes.label: Resolution of the Uncertainty Event
nodes.rationale: The document describes waiting for the uncertainty event to resolve before acting on a liquidity-driven decline.

nodes.label: Post-Risk Industry Rotation
nodes.rationale: After risk weakens, the document describes taking profit gradually and switching toward a newly confirmed industry direction.

nodes.label: Selloff Cause Determines Action
nodes.rationale: Liquidity pressure calls for waiting until uncertainty resolves before considering entry, while deterioration in business logic calls for exit without adding to the position.

nodes.label: Active Buying at a Loss
nodes.rationale: The document permits accepting an adverse technical setup only when industrial certainty is sufficiently high and all stated boundaries are met.

nodes.label: Industry Logic Unchanged
nodes.rationale: Orders, capacity, competition, policy direction, and management credibility are listed as checks for this boundary.

nodes.label: Liquidity Pressure Rather Than Logic Damage
nodes.rationale: The decline must be classified as liquidity pressure rather than damage to the fundamental logic, using the h16 process.
nodes.norm_label: liquidity pressure rather than logic damage

nodes.label: Predefined Stop-Loss Line
nodes.rationale: A price, event, or time stop-loss must be established in advance and not changed afterward.

nodes.label: Exit Triggers for Buying at a Loss
nodes.rationale: The stated triggers are valuation of the industry logic, easing liquidity pressure, thesis falsification, and emergence of a superior industry direction.
nodes.norm_label: exit triggers for buying at a loss

nodes.label: All Three Boundaries Are Required
nodes.rationale: The document explicitly states that active buying at a loss stops when any one of the three boundaries is missing.

nodes.label: Five-Layer AI Industry Framework
nodes.rationale: The framework divides the AI industry chain into energy, chips, computing power, large models, and applications.

nodes.label: AI Energy Layer
nodes.rationale: The energy layer covers power and power-computing coordination and is described as capital-intensive and long-cycle.

nodes.label: AI Chip Layer
nodes.rationale: The chip layer is characterized by technical barriers and domestic substitution.

nodes.label: AI Computing-Power Layer
nodes.rationale: The computing-power layer is characterized by expansion-investment drivers and a medium-fast pace.

nodes.label: AI Large-Model Layer
nodes.rationale: The large-model layer covers model training and AI infrastructure and is described as capital intensive.

nodes.label: AI Application Layer
nodes.rationale: The application layer concerns AI transformation across industries and is described as slow to penetrate and long term.

nodes.label: Three Elements Framework
nodes.rationale: The document uses this framework first to assess timing and then again for single-stock timing.

nodes.label: Timing-and-Layer Selection Integration
nodes.rationale: The stated sequence is to use the three elements for timing, use the five layers to select the investment layer, and then use the three elements again for stock timing.

nodes.label: Competition Structure Determinism
nodes.rationale: The retained core statement is that investment direction is hidden in national competition structure.

nodes.label: Bubble Defined by Lack of Future Growth
nodes.rationale: The v1.3 proposition recasts a bubble from high valuation to an absence of future hope or growth.
nodes.norm_label: bubble defined by lack of future growth

nodes.label: Historical Versus Future Certainty
nodes.rationale: The document reconciles stable historical cash-flow certainty with future growth certainty as a stage-dependent framework evolution rather than a contradiction.

nodes.label: New Money in New Industries
nodes.rationale: New money from central-bank release, foreign inflows, and new ETFs is described as being locked into the AI industry chain.

nodes.label: Old Money in Old Industries
nodes.rationale: The document describes capital sunk in property, liquor, banks, and insurance as old money eroded by inflation.

nodes.label: Directional Liquidity
nodes.rationale: The method updates liquidity analysis from aggregate quantity to direction, using flows, funds, and sector performance as indirect indicators.

nodes.label: AI Changes the Investor Competitive Environment
nodes.rationale: Model 9 is positioned as a meta-level reflection on how AI changes the environment in which investors themselves compete.
nodes.norm_label: ai changes the investor competitive environment

nodes.label: AI Distillation
nodes.rationale: The stated proposition is that AI distillation rapidly eliminates investment information asymmetry.

nodes.label: Investment Information Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: The document treats information asymmetry as being flattened by AI-enabled information efficiency.

nodes.label: Existing Investment-System Advantage
nodes.rationale: The document states that older concepts, experience, and investment systems can lose competitive advantage after AI distillation.

nodes.label: Human Comparative Advantage
nodes.rationale: The suggested human strengths are political economy, macro judgment, and risk perception.

nodes.label: AI Tool Scope Boundary
nodes.rationale: AI is stated to apply to information processing, data analysis, and announcement summaries, but not to geopolitical judgment, risk perception, long-term industry insight, or role-playing skill self-evaluation.

nodes.label: Meta-Level Supplement to Models 1–8
nodes.rationale: Model 9 is explicitly a supplement, not a replacement: it adds the question of how strong the AI-enabled opponent is when applying models 1–8.
